title: Common Network Protocols
intro: An independent 10–15 minute catch-up with feedback, unlimited retries and 80% mastery.

questions.prompt: What is a router's main job?

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read and follow the new material.

blocks.title: Protocols are rules
blocks.text: Communication protocols are agreed rules controlling how data is exchanged across a network.

blocks.title: Web and file protocols
blocks.text: HTTP transfers web pages; HTTPS uses encryption for secure web communication; FTP is used for file transfer.

blocks.title: Email protocols
blocks.text: SMTP sends email; POP downloads email to a client; IMAP accesses and synchronises server-based mail across devices.

blocks.title: TCP and IP
blocks.text: TCP helps ensure reliable, ordered delivery. IP supports addressing and routing so packets reach the intended destination.

blocks.title: Worked example
blocks.text: Sending and accessing messages are two separate jobs. SMTP is used to send outgoing email [1] from client towards email server [1]. IMAP accesses mail stored on a server [1], allowing messages to be synchronised across devices [1]. Name each protocol and link it to the specific email action.

items: Protocol — Rules for communication between devices.
HTTP — Hypertext Transfer Protocol, transfers web resources.
HTTPS — Secure HTTP with encrypted communication.
FTP — File Transfer Protocol, transfers files.
SMTP — Protocol used for sending email.
POP — Email-retrieval protocol often downloading mail locally.
IMAP — Email protocol for accessing and synchronising server-based email.
TCP — Provides reliable, ordered data delivery.
IP — Supports addressing and routing between networks.
